Good news for Kansas agriculture! 

USDA is investing nearly $4 million in Kansas meat processors to expand capacities and strengthen local processing opportunities for Kansas ranchers.

I’m especially pleased to see three of these investments in our Second Congressional District:

-Diamond A Processing (Junction City): $182,094
-Mitchell Bolling (Moran): $197,338
-Plainview Beef Company (Peabody): $2 million

These investments will support local businesses and improve opportunities for Kansas cattle producers.

Today, we honor the men and women who have served our nation. Their courage, sacrifice, and dedication deserve our gratitude every day.

Kansas has a special place in this holiday’s history. Emporia proudly holds the distinction of being the founding city of Veterans Day, a tradition that began in 1953 to honor all who served.

I was proud to recognize Emporia’s place in our nation’s history on the House floor.

To all our veterans and their families, thank you for your service and sacrifice.

Happy Veterans Day!

Good news for rural Kansas!

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is investing nearly $225.9 million MORE through the Rural Health Transformation Program for the coming year.

That’s an increase of $4 million above last year’s award for a two-year total of nearly $450 million--among the most for any state.

I was proud to vote for and support the legislation that established this program to deliver critical resources for rural healthcare providers and communities across Kansas.

Ensuring Kansans have access to quality healthcare, no matter where they live, remains an important priority. I’ll continue working to support rural communities across our state and especially in our 2nd Congressional District.

One of the joys of serving in Congress is the opportunity to nominate young Kansans to attend one of the U.S. service academies. Today we met with applicants at the Kansas Statehouse in Topeka. I always come away reassured that America's future will be in good hands. Thank you to all the students who are applying and to the families who support them.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
